questions.q: Find the next group: **ABD, BEG, CHJ, DKM, ?**
questions.solution: 1st letters A, B, C, D move +1, giving **E**. 2nd letters B, E, H, K move +3, giving **N**. 3rd letters D, G, J, M also move +3, giving **P**. Next group **ENP**.
questions.shortcut: Each position has its own constant step: +1, +3, +3.

questions.q: Find the next group: **ZA, YB, XC, ?**
questions.solution: First letters run backwards: Z, Y, X, **W**. Second letters run forwards: A, B, C, **D**. Next group **WD**.
questions.shortcut: Two counters moving in opposite directions.

questions.q: Find the next group: **AZ, BY, CX, ?**
questions.solution: First letters move forward: A, B, C, **D**; second letters move backward: Z, Y, X, **W**. Next group **DW**.

questions.q: Find the next group: **BDA, CEB, DFC, ?**
questions.solution: Every letter moves +1 across groups: B, C, D give **E**; D, E, F give **G**; A, B, C give **D**. Next group **EGD**.

questions.q: Find the next group: **ACX, BDW, CEV, ?**
questions.solution: 1st letters A, B, C go +1 → **D**; 2nd letters C, D, E go +1 → **F**; 3rd letters X, W, V go −1 → **U**. Next group **DFU**.

questions.q: **Book : Pages :: Ladder : ?**
questions.solution: A book is made up of pages; a ladder is made up of **rungs** (the horizontal steps). Wood is the material and climbing is the action, not the parts.

questions.q: **Bird : Nest :: Bee : ?**
questions.solution: A bird lives in a nest; a bee lives in a **hive**. Honey is the produce, swarm is the group and comb is only the storage structure inside.

questions.q: **SHOP : UJQR :: WARM : ?**
questions.solution: Each letter of SHOP moves +2: S to U, H to J, O to Q, P to R. Applying +2 to WARM: W to Y, A to C, R to T, M to O — **YCTO**.

questions.q: If **DUST** is coded as **64**, then **DISH** will be coded as
questions.solution: The code is the sum of the letter positions: D(4) + U(21) + S(19) + T(20) = 64. So DISH = 4 + 9 + 19 + 8 = **40**.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: **13, 17, 21, 23**
questions.solution: 13, 17 and 23 are prime numbers; 21 = 3 × 7 is not. Odd one: **21**.
questions.shortcut: Check divisibility by 3 and 7 first: 21 splits.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: **144, 196, 210, 256**
questions.solution: 144 = 12², 196 = 14² and 256 = 16² are perfect squares; 210 is not a square. Odd one: **210**.

questions.q: Pointing to a man, Rita said, **'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.'** How is the man related to Rita?
questions.solution: The only daughter of Rita's mother is Rita herself. So the man's mother is Rita — the man is Rita's **son**.
questions.shortcut: 'Only daughter of my mother' = the speaker (if the speaker is female).

questions.q: Read the symbols: **P + Q** means P is the mother of Q; **Q − R** means Q is the brother of R. In the expression **P + Q − R**, how is R related to P?
questions.solution: P is the mother of Q, and Q is the brother of R — siblings share parents, so R is also P's child. R is male, so R is P's **son** (not grandson — only one generation is described).

questions.q: **M** is the father of **N** and **P**. P is married to **L**, and L is the father of **K**. How is K related to N?
questions.solution: P is N's sister. K is P's daughter, so K is N's **niece**.

questions.q: Introducing a boy, a girl said, **'He is the son of my father's only son.'** How is the boy related to the girl?
questions.solution: The girl's father's only son is the girl's brother. The boy is that brother's son — the girl's **nephew**.
questions.shortcut: Father's only son = brother (of the girl).

questions.q:
If **÷** means **+**, **+** means **−**, **−** means **×** and **×** means **÷**, then find the value of

**15 ÷ 3 + 10 − 2 × 4**
questions.solution: After substitution: 15 + 3 − 10 × 2 ÷ 4. BODMAS: × and ÷ first — 10 × 2 = 20, 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Then 15 + 3 − 5 = **13**. (The original expression without substitution gives 7 — a trap.)

questions.q: Which pair of signs, used in order, makes **8 _ 4 _ 2 = 30** correct?
questions.solution: Test the choices: 8 × 4 − 2 = 32 − 2 = **30**. No other pair of signs gives 30 (8 × 4 + 2 = 34, 8 + 4 × 2 = 16, 8 − 4 + 2 = 6, and so on).
questions.shortcut: Try × first with each second sign; 32 needs −2.

questions.q: Six friends **A, B, C, D, E and F** sit in a row facing north. **A** sits second from the left end, **B** sits adjacent to **A**, **C** sits third to the right of **B**, and **D** sits at the right end. **E** is not an immediate neighbour of **D**. Who sits **second from the right end**?
questions.solution: A is at seat 2. B adjacent to A; C = B + 3 forces B to seat 1 (if B were at seat 3, C would need seat 6, which D occupies). So B is at seat 1, C at seat 4, D at seat 6. E cannot touch D, so E takes seat 3, leaving F at seat 5. Row: B, A, E, C, F, D. Second from the right = **F**.
questions.shortcut: The C = B + 3 clue pins B's side first.

questions.q:
**Statements:** No cat is a dog. All dogs are animals.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some animals are cats.
II. No dog is a cat.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution: 'No cat is a dog' works both ways, so II (**follows**). I is only possible, not certain — cats may sit inside or outside the animals circle, so it **does not follow**. Answer: **Only II**.
questions.shortcut: Negative premises are symmetric; possibility is not a conclusion.

questions.q:
Arrange as per the dictionary and pick the word that comes **in the middle**:

**Temple, Tenant, Tell, Ten, Temper**
questions.solution: Dictionary order: **Tell, Temper, Temple, Ten, Tenant**. After 'te', the third letter decides: l < m < n. Among the m-words, Temper < Temple (fourth letter e < l). Among the n-words, Ten < Tenant (a word comes before its own extensions). The middle (third) word is **Ten**.
questions.shortcut: Sort by the first differing letter, then by length.

questions.q: **Sita** walks 6 km towards east, then turns left and walks 8 km, and then turns left again and walks 6 km. How far and in which direction is she from her starting point?
questions.solution: East 6, left → north 8, left → west 6. The 6 km east and 6 km west cancel, leaving **8 km North**.

questions.q: In a class of students, **Mohan ranks 8th from the top** and **37th from the bottom**. How many students are there in the class?
questions.solution: Total = top rank + bottom rank − 1 (Mohan is counted twice) = 8 + 37 − 1 = **44**.
questions.shortcut: Rank from top + rank from bottom − 1.
